implementationPlan.description: Write the three arms in tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts as a new `graphContentCases` array, following `codecCases` in structure and comment discipline. The subject is landed and green: `encodeGraphContent` / `decodeGraphContent` from the bare `@moe/scheduler` root -- go through the published codec, never `canonicalGraphJson` or the raw hash, which are deliberately withheld so no consumer can mint bytes the kernel never accepted. `GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS` has three members (GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, GRAPH_VALIDATION) and `GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES` offers DIGEST_MISMATCH, MALFORMED, NONCANONICAL, NOT_BYTES, TOO_LARGE, UNREADABLE and UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA. Suggested shape, and PREFER SPREADING THE THREE LAYER MEMBERS ACROSS THE THREE ARMS so the whole constant is exercised rather than one member three times: BEFORE -- bytes that never become content (truncated or not-bytes) refusing at GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, where nothing later on the path is reachable; FORGED/AFTER -- encode a valid content, then carry its digest onto a different content so shape and canonicalisation both pass and ONLY the re-derived digest comparison can refuse, at GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, with the `integrity` thunk re-sealing through production and asserted ok:true first; RACE -- a re-spelled canonical encoding raced against a non-canonical or duplicate-key variant. Assert the exact code AND layer on every arm, never merely that the call failed. Then spread `graphContentCases` into `INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES` at :1204.
implementationPlan.note:
FOUR ARMS WRITTEN and spread into INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES (now fourteen arrays). Four, not three: the plan asked me to prefer spreading the three declared layer members across the arms, and GRAPH_VALIDATION cannot ride the RACE arm — a race case asserts only that neither leg was admitted and pins no code or layer at all. So the constant gets two BEFORE arms.

- BEFORE `canonical graph-content bytes truncated mid-envelope` -> GRAPH_CONTENT_UNREADABLE @ GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC. `decodeGraphContent(sealed.bytes.slice(0, 40))`; 40 bytes lands inside the `hash` string so the input never becomes one JSON document. Exactly two guards sit earlier (NOT_BYTES, TOO_LARGE) and both ADMIT it, which is why the bounded read is provably the branch that answered.
- BEFORE `a structurally invalid snapshot keeps the graph kernel's own code` -> GRAPH_SELF_EDGE @ GRAPH_VALIDATION. `encodeGraphContent` over the chain plus one HARD self edge. This is the passthrough branch, and the expected code is the KERNEL's rather than any GRAPH_CONTENT_* member, so the arm reddens if a structural failure is ever restamped as a codec failure. Single-issue by construction: validate-graph.ts:18-24 evaluates cycle and completion-closure only once integrity holds.
- FORGED/AFTER `one content's sealed hash carried onto a different content` -> GRAPH_CONTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH @ GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY. Content B's canonical bytes with content A's production hash substituted; shape, schema tag, field read and the completion reconciliation all still pass, and the digest recompute runs BEFORE the canonical re-encode (graph-content.ts:216 vs :224), so IDENTITY answers with a mismatch rather than the misleading NONCANONICAL. `integrity` thunk re-encodes BOTH halves through production and asserts the forged bytes equal exactly the carrier's own sealed bytes with the donor's production hash spliced in.
- RACE `a re-spelled envelope races a duplicated hash key` through `probeRacing(RACE_BOUND, ...)` via the `racing` helper: left = envelope keys reversed (still parses, key check is a SET, digest still matches, so only the canonical re-encode can answer), right = a duplicated `hash` key where JSON.parse keeps the last.

SUPPORT CODE. `soleIssue` projects production's own `code`/`layer` up from `{ok:false, issues:[...]}`, which `assertRefusedWith` cannot read and `asLayered` does not cover; it THROWS when production answered with more than one issue, because picking issues[0] would silently pin whichever `sortIssues` ordered first and the case would be asserting a branch it never arranged. All hostile input is plain object literals handed to production unjudged, and every byte string forged is derived from bytes production itself sealed — only `encodeGraphContent`/`decodeGraphContent` are called, never the withheld `canonicalGraphJson` or `graphContentDigest`.
